fieldValues.title: The clerk's runtime imports nothing outside Node's standard library
fieldValues.decision_question: May the clerk's runtime code depend on npm packages?
fieldValues.context: Proposed from /ship clerk#97 (clerk serve). The plan for clerk serve named ajv as its one runtime dependency, to validate requests against api/openapi.json. srs-programme's workflows (programme-validate, upkeep, board sync, roadmap) and the cloud routines run `node bin/clerk.mjs` from a bare checkout with no npm install. A runtime dependency would break every one of them, silently until it ran. It follows the clerk's existing practice: every clerk command already runs from a bare checkout, and lib/practice is kept pure for srs-web (clerk/CLAUDE.md).
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: Allow runtime dependencies and add `npm ci` to every workflow and routine: every caller gains an install step and a network fetch, and a missed one breaks only when it runs. Scope the rule to the code the workflows and routines run, and let clerk serve (on the owner's desktop, where `npm ci` is cheap) have dependencies: clerk serve imports the same lib/adapters and lib/practice the workflows run, so a dependency added for it would creep into shared modules, and the line between the two would need a guard of its own. Vendor the dependencies into the repository: copied code to keep current. Do nothing: nothing stops the next change from adding one, and the break shows first in a scheduled job.
fieldValues.decision_statement: The clerk's runtime (bin, lib and scripts) imports only Node built-ins and its own modules. npm packages are devDependencies, used by tests only.
fieldValues.rationale: Every caller of the clerk runs it from a bare checkout, and should be able to keep doing so. Where a package would help at runtime, the clerk derives what it needs from its own sources instead: clerk serve checks query parameters from the spec, and refuses at startup any rule it cannot enforce. The tests use ajv to validate every response against the full spec.
fieldValues.revisit_when: When a runtime need cannot be met from the standard library at reasonable cost, or the workflows and routines gain a shared install step.
fieldValues.next_steps: Enforced by test/runtime-imports.test.mjs in the clerk (clerk#97).
